intent: Make report popovers and block-local details mutually exclusive; close every contextual layer by outside click or Escape, while synchronizing aria-expanded and restoring trigger focus where applicable.
Keep the language control out of permanent report chrome and expose it inside the report-view settings menu with a visible current-locale summary.
Reduce top-chrome competition by shortening the page title and placing the context toolbar on the trailing side of the report tabs rather than on a separate third row.
Use distinct semantic icons for report inspector, KPI configuration, chart tuning, filters, and each analytical navigation destination.
Move Pipelines out of Results and consolidate the pilot-level Data Foundation and Administration shortcuts into one meaningful Data & Management group without removing their product surfaces.
Adopt a Linear Graphite shell over a Midnight Analytics data surface: black canvas, elevated rounded workspace, restrained graphite hierarchy, and low-cardinality borders.
Turn the sidebar into persistent collapsible navigation groups and preserve the complete Analytics information architecture.

Use anchored local popovers for period, comparison, stores, filters, view, KPI, and chart settings while reserving the docked right inspector for context, discussion, trust, saved views, and share actions.
Represent KPI as a compact analytical property row with separators rather than cards or a hero block.
Restore the complete analytics navigation, including Sales and Products & Categories.
Use Apache ECharts with SVG rendering for analytical visuals and provide a data-table alternative for every chart.

Support plan and multi-year comparison series for 2024, 2023, and 2022; keep the KPI primary comparison separate from lifecycle-table value format, percent denominator, comparison target, base, and delta-display controls.

Pivot the Lifecycle table to channel and segment rows with time buckets as columns; expose Customers, Revenue, Average receipt, and Frequency metrics plus independent Values or Percent, denominator, comparison, base, and delta-display axes.
Restore the slide-out report-context drawer with link sharing and email preflight.
Use one boundary toggle for the report inspector; on desktop allocate a right grid column and reflow the report without translate, while narrow Web keeps an overlay.
Use a 48 px metric rail with eight useful defaults and a user-orderable twelve-metric compatible library instead of a large KPI hero.
Make the reviewed finding optional and keep a common metric schema across segment profiles.
Replace synthetic narrative cards in Dynamics with value-labelled charts and explicit table alternatives.
Preserve annual customer frequency without synthesizing a per-month unit.
Use K, M, and MM abbreviations consistently in Russian analytical visuals.
Provide native SVG and two-times PNG export actions for every ECharts visual.
Give Focus an adaptive 60–70vh chart region with readable labels and keep graph plus full table in one vertically scrollable analysis surface.
Give ordinary controls borderless base, hover, active, and keyboard-focus states.

Separate monthly metric selection from Line/Bars visualization choice, expose that choice through the same chart-settings icon used on Overview and Segments, and preserve the selected type across metric, table, and focus transitions.

Use one focus registry for lifecycle composition, monthly dynamics, quarterly contribution, and segment size, with source-specific title, option, table, export, URL identity, Escape handling, and focus restoration.
Allow an explicit actual-only state with no comparison series, disabled primary-comparison controls, no KPI deltas, and no synthetic lifecycle delta column.
Keep store scope local to one Stores popover and one state source; remove store duplication from general and inspector filters.
Separate quick single-dimension filters from advanced multi-condition filtering with AND/OR logic, removal, reset, and one applied-state summary.
Define Copy Link and email preflight as the same immutable snapshot-link contract containing tab, period, comparison, stores, and applied filters, with recipient access required and no real delivery.
Use customer-base trend small multiples as the stable Overview default; retain task-constrained snapshot columns, 100% composition, heatmap, and exact table representations.
Separate report scope filters from a Break down by control for Channel and Store, using vertically stacked small multiples with shared scales and full-breakdown tables.
Open one shared Focus surface from chart or table controls at the corresponding section, preserve graph and table together, trap modal focus, and restore the originating control on exit.
Align the report-inspector header and navigation row exactly with the report page header and report navigation row, and give the desktop inspector a 420 px working width.
Suppress native-select focus decoration only after pointer input while preserving the visible keyboard focus ring through explicit input-modality state.

Replace the narrow condition list with an entity-grouped searchable filter catalog, explicit nested AND/OR groups, visible system and inherited scope, draft expression, preview estimate, and separate applied state.
Provide one report-level day, week, month, quarter, or year period/comparison default plus explicit inherit or local overrides on every chart and table block.
Render segment size against block-local comparison periods and replace selected migrations with a complete directed 5 by 5 transition matrix, including stayed cells and comparison deltas.

Replace the ambiguous General period label with explicit As report inheritance and make month, quarter, and year select different bucket boundaries, aggregates, chart points, table rows, and CSV rows.
Move the typed filter builder to a dedicated top-level Inspector tab and keep the snapshot share surface compact with two primary actions and disclosure-only resolved state.

Apply a versioned visual style template at report level with per-chart overrides for palette, contrast, chart type scale, and table density, while keeping the template builder as a separate Settings destination.
Use contrast-aware heatmap labels and expose permission-safe report author, update, and publication metadata in Notes and Methodology and snapshot state.

Replace select-heavy local strips with icon commands that group data and period, comparison, grouping, and palette settings; show local overrides with an accent marker and expose accessible names plus tooltips.
Use a hierarchy data-model icon for grouping, separate one shared metric label from channel facet titles, and prevent repeated metric names or overlapping group captions.

Separate data palette from chart background and interface theme, and place report-wide S/M/L controls for primary values, data labels, axes and legend, and table text in one permanently discoverable toolbar menu.
Use compact K, M, and MM labels consistently across chart types and tabs while retaining exact values in tooltips and analytical tables.
Keep Chart/Table as the only visible representation switch on Overview, Dynamics, and Segments; place Line/Bars and Horizontal/Vertical chart choices in one shared chart-settings pattern.
Allow a user-scoped, versioned personal analysis view to save and restore the complete fixture configuration without changing the published view.
Treat report grouping as an ordered, extensible dimension list with add, remove, and reorder actions; render the first dimension as sections and subsequent dimensions as the nested row hierarchy.
Align year comparisons by corresponding month and quarter rather than comparing every visible bucket to one unrelated selected bucket.
Place the report data palette and all analytical text-size controls in one Appearance plane and remove duplicated block-local palette menus.
Use native rounded command clusters with one 16 px analytical-control radius across report tabs, context chips, segmented switches, and block commands.
Use equal-width numeric table columns and one value-contrast token across Overview, Lifecycle, and Segment tables; avoid a separate wide-screen Lifecycle scroll surface.
Show compact actual, plan, and historical labels for every Segment bar and make analytical value presets materially change the rendered SVG label size.
Use one compact report-wide S/M/L choice for all analytical text instead of independent size controls for values, labels, axes, and tables.
Render toolbar actions as borderless rounded groups with hover and active feedback on the individual command while retaining keyboard focus visibility.
Give every grouped facet explicit shared value-axis bounds and unique stack identities so channels remain comparable and every stacked series starts at zero.
Show readable labels for actual, plan, and historical quarterly stacks, moving the small top segment label outside the stack when needed.
Increase grouped Segment chart row and bar spacing with the selected analytical size and hide residual SVG label overlap.
Apply the one report-wide S/M/L analytical-size state to tables in both ordinary and shared Focus surfaces.
Expose the selected analytical size as a complete pressed pill with an accent marker, a distinct selected hover state, tooltip text, and a selected-state accessible name.
Standardize table data, group, and header row heights across Overview, Lifecycle, Dynamics, and Segment representations for every S/M/L preset.
Bound ordinary analytical panels to a centered readable width, restore their visual surface boundary, and reserve chart gutters for complete end labels.
Use one download-icon menu per reportable block; Chart mode offers PNG and SVG while Table mode automatically offers XLSX and CSV.
Provide XLSX and CSV export for every standalone and focus table, and PNG and SVG export for every ordinary and focus chart.
Open the report inspector from a rounded top-right slider control and render the inspector as a rounded trailing desktop pane or viewport-contained narrow overlay.

Give simultaneously visible tables with the same trailing analytical columns one shared grid: a maximum-content semantic stub and identical value-column tracks, independent of row content, grouping depth, locale, or S/M/L size.

Move high-cardinality chart series into one adaptive external sibling panel with localized latest values, metric by scenario factorization, synchronized visibility state, Focus and export parity, and a readable right-or-lower placement.

Replace the wide persistent sidebar with one compact icon rail and a reusable contextual flyout or narrow drawer that preserves hierarchy, changes sections in place, overlays rather than resizes the desktop workspace, and has complete keyboard and modal behavior.
